\(5x + 3y = 9\) . . . (I)

\(2x - 3y = 12\) . . . (II)

Adding equations (I) and (II) the \(y\)-terms cancel:

\(7x = 21\) \(\therefore x = 3\)

Place \(x = 3\) in equation (I):

\(5 \times 3 + 3y = 9\) \(\therefore 15 + 3y = 9\) \(\therefore 3y = 9 - 15 = -6\)

\(\therefore y = \dfrac{-6}{3} = -2\)

\(\therefore\) Solution is \((x, y) = (3, -2)\).

\(3a + 5b = 26\) . . . (I)

\(a + 5b = 22\) . . . (II)

Subtracting equation (II) from equation (I) the \(5b\) terms cancel:

\((3a - a) + (5b - 5b) = 26 - 22\) \(\therefore 2a = 4\) \(\therefore a = 2\)

Placing \(a = 2\) in equation (II): \(2 + 5b = 22\) \(\therefore 5b = 20\) \(\therefore b = 4\)

\(\therefore (a, b) = (2, 4)\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(x + 7y = 10\) . . . (I)

\(3x - 2y = 7\) . . . (II)

From equation (I), \(x = 10 - 7y\). Substituting in equation (II):

\(3(10 - 7y) - 2y = 7\) \(\therefore 30 - 21y - 2y = 7\) \(\therefore -23y = -23\) \(\therefore y = 1\)

\(\therefore x = 10 - 7 \times 1 = 3\)

\(\therefore (x, y) = (3, 1)\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(2x - 3y = 9\) . . . (I)

\(2x + y = 13\) . . . (II)

Subtracting equation (II) from equation (I) the \(2x\) terms cancel:

\(-3y - y = 9 - 13\) \(\therefore -4y = -4\) \(\therefore y = 1\)

Placing \(y = 1\) in equation (II): \(2x + 1 = 13\) \(\therefore 2x = 12\) \(\therefore x = 6\)

\(\therefore (x, y) = (6, 1)\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(5m - 3n = 19\) . . . (I)

\(m - 6n = -7\) . . . (II)

Multiplying equation (I) by 2: \(10m - 6n = 38\) . . . (III)

Subtracting equation (II) from equation (III): \(9m = 45\) \(\therefore m = 5\)

Placing \(m = 5\) in equation (II): \(5 - 6n = -7\) \(\therefore -6n = -12\) \(\therefore n = 2\)

\(\therefore (m, n) = (5, 2)\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(5x + 2y = -3\) . . . (I)

\(x + 5y = 4\) . . . (II)

From equation (II), \(x = 4 - 5y\). Substituting in equation (I):

\(5(4 - 5y) + 2y = -3\) \(\therefore 20 - 25y + 2y = -3\) \(\therefore -23y = -23\) \(\therefore y = 1\)

\(\therefore x = 4 - 5 \times 1 = -1\)

\(\therefore (x, y) = (-1, 1)\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(\dfrac{1}{3}x + y = \dfrac{10}{3}\) . . . (I)

\(2x + \dfrac{1}{4}y = \dfrac{11}{4}\) . . . (II)

Multiplying equation (I) by 3 and equation (II) by 4 to clear the fractions:

\(x + 3y = 10\) . . . (III)

\(8x + y = 11\) . . . (IV)

From equation (IV), \(y = 11 - 8x\). Substituting in equation (III):

\(x + 3(11 - 8x) = 10\) \(\therefore x + 33 - 24x = 10\) \(\therefore -23x = -23\) \(\therefore x = 1\)

\(\therefore y = 11 - 8 = 3\)

\(\therefore (x, y) = (1, 3)\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(99x + 101y = 499\) . . . (I)

\(101x + 99y = 501\) . . . (II)

The coefficients of \(x\) and \(y\) are interchanged, so add and subtract the equations.

Adding: \(200x + 200y = 1000\) \(\therefore x + y = 5\) . . . (III)

Subtracting equation (II) from equation (I): \(-2x + 2y = -2\) \(\therefore -x + y = -1\) . . . (IV)

Adding equations (III) and (IV): \(2y = 4\) \(\therefore y = 2\), and then \(x = 5 - 2 = 3\)

\(\therefore (x, y) = (3, 2)\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(49x - 57y = 172\) . . . (I)

\(57x - 49y = 252\) . . . (II)

The coefficients of \(x\) and \(y\) are interchanged (with signs), so add and subtract.

Adding: \(106x - 106y = 424\) \(\therefore x - y = 4\) . . . (III)

Subtracting equation (II) from equation (I): \(-8x - 8y = -80\) \(\therefore x + y = 10\) . . . (IV)

Adding equations (III) and (IV): \(2x = 14\) \(\therefore x = 7\), and then \(y = 10 - 7 = 3\)

\(\therefore (x, y) = (7, 3)\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

When \(y = 3\): \(x + 3 = 3\) \(\therefore x = 0\).

| \(y\) | 0 | 5 | 3 |
| \((x, y)\) | (3, 0) | (\(-2\), 5) | (0, 3) |

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

| \(x\) | 4 | \(-1\) | 0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(y\) | 0 | \(-5\) | \(-4\) |
| \((x, y)\) | (4, 0) | (\(-1\), \(-5\)) | (0, \(-4\)) |

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

For a determinant \(\begin{vmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{vmatrix}\) the value is \(ad - bc\), so here \(a = 3\), \(b = 2\), \(c = 4\), \(d = 5\).

\(\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 3 \times 5 - 2 \times 4 = 15 - 8 = 7\)

\(\therefore\) the four blanks are 5, 2, 15 and 7 in that order.

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(\begin{vmatrix} -1 & 7 \\ 2 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = (-1)(4) - (7)(2) = -4 - 14 = -18\)

\(\therefore\) the value of the determinant is \(-18\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(\begin{vmatrix} 5 & 3 \\ -7 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = (5)(0) - (3)(-7) = 0 + 21 = 21\)

\(\therefore\) the value of the determinant is 21.

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(\begin{vmatrix} \dfrac{7}{3} & \dfrac{5}{3} \\ \dfrac{3}{2} & \dfrac{1}{2} \end{vmatrix} = \dfrac{7}{3} \times \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{5}{3} \times \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{7}{6} - \dfrac{15}{6} = \dfrac{-8}{6}\)

\(\therefore\) the value of the determinant is \(-\dfrac{4}{3}\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

Write the equations in the form \(ax + by = c\):

\(3x - 4y = 10\) . . . (I)

\(4x + 3y = 5\) . . . (II)

\(\mathrm{D} = \begin{vmatrix} 3 & -4 \\ 4 & 3 \end{vmatrix} = 9 - (-16) = 25\)

\(\mathrm{D}_x = \begin{vmatrix} 10 & -4 \\ 5 & 3 \end{vmatrix} = 30 - (-20) = 50\)

\(\mathrm{D}_y = \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 10 \\ 4 & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 15 - 40 = -25\)

By Cramer's rule, \(x = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_x}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{50}{25} = 2\) and \(y = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_y}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{-25}{25} = -1\)

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(\therefore (x, y) = (2, -1)\).

Rewrite both equations in the form \(ax + by = c\): \(4x + 3y - 4 = 0\) becomes \(4x + 3y = 4\), and \(6x = 8 - 5y\) becomes \(6x + 5y = 8\).

\(4x + 3y = 4\) . . . (I)

\(6x + 5y = 8\) . . . (II)

\(\mathrm{D} = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 3 \\ 6 & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 20 - 18 = 2\)

\(\mathrm{D}_x = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 3 \\ 8 & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 20 - 24 = -4\)

\(\mathrm{D}_y = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 4 \\ 6 & 8 \end{vmatrix} = 32 - 24 = 8\)

By Cramer's rule, \(x = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_x}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{-4}{2} = -2\) and \(y = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_y}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{8}{2} = 4\)

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(\therefore (x, y) = (-2, 4)\).

Write the equations in the form \(ax + by = c\):

\(x + 2y = -1\) . . . (I)

\(2x - 3y = 12\) . . . (II)

\(\mathrm{D} = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 \end{vmatrix} = -3 - 4 = -7\)

\(\mathrm{D}_x = \begin{vmatrix} -1 & 2 \\ 12 & -3 \end{vmatrix} = 3 - 24 = -21\)

\(\mathrm{D}_y = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 12 \end{vmatrix} = 12 + 2 = 14\)

By Cramer's rule, \(x = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_x}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{-21}{-7} = 3\) and \(y = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_y}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{14}{-7} = -2\)

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(\therefore (x, y) = (3, -2)\).

Write the equations in the form \(ax + by = c\):

\(6x - 4y = -12\) . . . (I)

\(8x - 3y = -2\) . . . (II)

\(\mathrm{D} = \begin{vmatrix} 6 & -4 \\ 8 & -3 \end{vmatrix} = -18 + 32 = 14\)

\(\mathrm{D}_x = \begin{vmatrix} -12 & -4 \\ -2 & -3 \end{vmatrix} = 36 - 8 = 28\)

\(\mathrm{D}_y = \begin{vmatrix} 6 & -12 \\ 8 & -2 \end{vmatrix} = -12 + 96 = 84\)

By Cramer's rule, \(x = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_x}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{28}{14} = 2\) and \(y = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_y}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{84}{14} = 6\)

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(\therefore (x, y) = (2, 6)\).

Write the equations in the form \(ax + by = c\):

\(4m + 6n = 54\) . . . (I)

\(3m + 2n = 28\) . . . (II)

\(\mathrm{D} = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 6 \\ 3 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 8 - 18 = -10\)

\(\mathrm{D}_m = \begin{vmatrix} 54 & 6 \\ 28 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = 108 - 168 = -60\)

\(\mathrm{D}_n = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 54 \\ 3 & 28 \end{vmatrix} = 112 - 162 = -50\)

By Cramer's rule, \(m = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_m}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{-60}{-10} = 6\) and \(n = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_n}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{-50}{-10} = 5\)

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(\therefore (m, n) = (6, 5)\).

Write the second equation as \(x - \dfrac{1}{2}y = \dfrac{1}{2}\), so \(a_2 = 1\), \(b_2 = -\dfrac{1}{2}\), \(c_2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

\(2x + 3y = 2\) . . . (I)

\(x - \dfrac{1}{2}y = \dfrac{1}{2}\) . . . (II)

\(\mathrm{D} = \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 1 & -\dfrac{1}{2} \end{vmatrix} = -1 - 3 = -4\)

\(\mathrm{D}_x = \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ \dfrac{1}{2} & -\dfrac{1}{2} \end{vmatrix} = -1 - \dfrac{3}{2} = -\dfrac{5}{2}\)

\(\mathrm{D}_y = \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 2 \\ 1 & \dfrac{1}{2} \end{vmatrix} = 1 - 2 = -1\)

By Cramer's rule, \(x = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_x}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{-5/2}{-4} = \dfrac{5}{8}\) and \(y = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_y}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{-1}{-4} = \dfrac{1}{4}\)

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(\therefore (x, y) = \left(\dfrac{5}{8},\ \dfrac{1}{4}\right)\).

Put \(m = \dfrac{1}{x}\) and \(n = \dfrac{1}{y}\).

\(2m - 3n = 15\) . . . (I)

\(8m + 5n = 77\) . . . (II)

Multiplying equation (I) by 4: \(8m - 12n = 60\) . . . (III)

Subtracting equation (III) from equation (II): \(17n = 17\) \(\therefore n = 1\)

From equation (I): \(2m = 15 + 3 = 18\) \(\therefore m = 9\)

\(m = \dfrac{1}{x} = 9\) \(\therefore x = \dfrac{1}{9}\); \(n = \dfrac{1}{y} = 1\) \(\therefore y = 1\)

\(\therefore (x, y) = \left(\dfrac{1}{9},\ 1\right)\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

Put \(m = \dfrac{1}{x + y}\) and \(n = \dfrac{1}{x - y}\).

\(10m + 2n = 4\), i.e. \(5m + n = 2\) . . . (I)

\(15m - 5n = -2\) . . . (II)

From equation (I), \(n = 2 - 5m\). Substituting in equation (II):

\(15m - 5(2 - 5m) = -2\) \(\therefore 15m - 10 + 25m = -2\) \(\therefore 40m = 8\) \(\therefore m = \dfrac{1}{5}\)

\(\therefore n = 2 - 1 = 1\)

\(\dfrac{1}{x + y} = \dfrac{1}{5}\) \(\therefore x + y = 5\); \(\dfrac{1}{x - y} = 1\) \(\therefore x - y = 1\)

Adding: \(2x = 6\) \(\therefore x = 3\), \(y = 2\)

\(\therefore (x, y) = (3, 2)\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

Put \(a = \dfrac{1}{x - 2}\) and \(b = \dfrac{1}{y + 3}\).

\(27a + 31b = 85\) . . . (I)

\(31a + 27b = 89\) . . . (II)

The coefficients are interchanged, so add and subtract.

Adding: \(58a + 58b = 174\) \(\therefore a + b = 3\) . . . (III)

Subtracting equation (I) from equation (II): \(4a - 4b = 4\) \(\therefore a - b = 1\) . . . (IV)

From (III) and (IV): \(a = 2\), \(b = 1\)

\(\dfrac{1}{x - 2} = 2\) \(\therefore x - 2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\) \(\therefore x = \dfrac{5}{2}\)

\(\dfrac{1}{y + 3} = 1\) \(\therefore y + 3 = 1\) \(\therefore y = -2\)

\(\therefore (x, y) = \left(\dfrac{5}{2},\ -2\right)\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

Put \(m = \dfrac{1}{3x + y}\) and \(n = \dfrac{1}{3x - y}\).

\(m + n = \dfrac{3}{4}\) . . . (I)

\(\dfrac{m}{2} - \dfrac{n}{2} = -\dfrac{1}{8}\), i.e. \(m - n = -\dfrac{1}{4}\) . . . (II)

Adding: \(2m = \dfrac{1}{2}\) \(\therefore m = \dfrac{1}{4}\); then \(n = \dfrac{3}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}\)

\(\dfrac{1}{3x + y} = \dfrac{1}{4}\) \(\therefore 3x + y = 4\)

\(\dfrac{1}{3x - y} = \dfrac{1}{2}\) \(\therefore 3x - y = 2\)

Adding: \(6x = 6\) \(\therefore x = 1\), \(y = 1\)

\(\therefore (x, y) = (1, 1)\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

In a rectangle the opposite sides are equal, so the two lengths are equal and the two breadths are equal.

\(2x + y + 8 = 4x - y\) \(\therefore 2x - 2y = 8\) \(\therefore x - y = 4\) . . . (I)

\(x + 4 = 2y\) \(\therefore x - 2y = -4\) . . . (II)

Subtracting equation (II) from equation (I): \(y = 8\); then from equation (I) \(x = 12\).

\(\therefore x = 12\), \(y = 8\).

Length \(= 4x - y = 48 - 8 = 40\) units and breadth \(= x + 4 = 16\) units (check: \(2y = 16\) and \(2x + y + 8 = 40\)).

Perimeter \(= 2(40 + 16) = 112\) units.

Area \(= 40 \times 16 = 640\) sq. units.

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

Let the father's present age be \(x\) years and the son's present age be \(y\) years.

From the first condition: \(x + 2y = 70\) . . . (I)

From the second condition: \(2x + y = 95\) . . . (II)

Multiplying equation (I) by 2: \(2x + 4y = 140\) . . . (III)

Subtracting equation (II) from equation (III): \(3y = 45\) \(\therefore y = 15\)

From equation (I): \(x = 70 - 30 = 40\)

\(\therefore\) the father is 40 years old and the son is 15 years old.

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

Let the numerator be \(x\) and the denominator be \(y\).

From the first condition: \(y = 2x + 4\) . . . (I)

From the second condition: \(y - 6 = 12(x - 6)\) . . . (II)

Substituting equation (I) in equation (II):

\(2x + 4 - 6 = 12x - 72\) \(\therefore 2x - 2 = 12x - 72\) \(\therefore 70 = 10x\) \(\therefore x = 7\)

\(\therefore y = 2 \times 7 + 4 = 18\)

\(\therefore\) the fraction is \(\dfrac{7}{18}\).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

Let the weight of one box of type A be \(x\) kg and of one box of type B be \(y\) kg. The truck's capacity is 10 tons \(= 10000\) kg.

From the first condition: \(150x + 100y = 10000\), i.e. \(3x + 2y = 200\) . . . (I)

From the second condition: \(260x + 40y = 10000\), i.e. \(13x + 2y = 500\) . . . (II)

Subtracting equation (I) from equation (II): \(10x = 300\) \(\therefore x = 30\)

From equation (I): \(2y = 200 - 90 = 110\) \(\therefore y = 55\)

\(\therefore\) a box of type A weighs 30 kg and a box of type B weighs 55 kg.

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

Let the distance travelled by bus be \(x\) km. Then the distance travelled by aeroplane is \((1900 - x)\) km.

Time \(= \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}}\), and the total time is 5 hours.

\(\dfrac{x}{60} + \dfrac{1900 - x}{700} = 5\)

Multiplying throughout by 4200 (the L.C.M. of 60 and 700):

\(70x + 6(1900 - x) = 21000\) \(\therefore 70x + 11400 - 6x = 21000\) \(\therefore 64x = 9600\) \(\therefore x = 150\)

\(\therefore\) Vishal travelled 150 km by bus (and 1750 km by aeroplane).

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

Write \(3x + 5y - 8 = 0\) as \(3x + 5y = 8\).

\(6x - 3y = -10\) . . . (I)

\(3x + 5y = 8\) . . . (II)

\(\mathrm{D} = \begin{vmatrix} 6 & -3 \\ 3 & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 30 + 9 = 39\)

\(\mathrm{D}_x = \begin{vmatrix} -10 & -3 \\ 8 & 5 \end{vmatrix} = -50 + 24 = -26\)

\(\mathrm{D}_y = \begin{vmatrix} 6 & -10 \\ 3 & 8 \end{vmatrix} = 48 + 30 = 78\)

By Cramer's rule, \(x = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_x}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{-26}{39} = -\dfrac{2}{3}\) and \(y = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_y}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{78}{39} = 2\)

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(\therefore (x, y) = \left(-\dfrac{2}{3},\ 2\right)\).

Write the equations in the form \(ax + by = c\):

\(4m - 2n = -4\) . . . (I)

\(4m + 3n = 16\) . . . (II)

\(\mathrm{D} = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & -2 \\ 4 & 3 \end{vmatrix} = 12 + 8 = 20\)

\(\mathrm{D}_m = \begin{vmatrix} -4 & -2 \\ 16 & 3 \end{vmatrix} = -12 + 32 = 20\)

\(\mathrm{D}_n = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & -4 \\ 4 & 16 \end{vmatrix} = 64 + 16 = 80\)

By Cramer's rule, \(m = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_m}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{20}{20} = 1\) and \(n = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_n}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{80}{20} = 4\)

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

Write the equations in the form \(ax + by = c\):

\(3x - 2y = \dfrac{5}{2}\) . . . (I)

\(\dfrac{1}{3}x + 3y = -\dfrac{4}{3}\) . . . (II)

\(\mathrm{D} = \begin{vmatrix} 3 & -2 \\ \dfrac{1}{3} & 3 \end{vmatrix} = 9 + \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{29}{3}\)

\(\mathrm{D}_x = \begin{vmatrix} \dfrac{5}{2} & -2 \\ -\dfrac{4}{3} & 3 \end{vmatrix} = \dfrac{15}{2} - \dfrac{8}{3} = \dfrac{29}{6}\)

\(\mathrm{D}_y = \begin{vmatrix} 3 & \dfrac{5}{2} \\ \dfrac{1}{3} & -\dfrac{4}{3} \end{vmatrix} = -4 - \dfrac{5}{6} = -\dfrac{29}{6}\)

By Cramer's rule, \(x = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_x}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{29/6}{29/3} = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(y = \dfrac{\mathrm{D}_y}{\mathrm{D}} = \dfrac{-29/6}{29/3} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\)

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

\(\therefore (x, y) = \left(\dfrac{1}{2},\ -\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\).

\(\mathrm{D}_y = \begin{vmatrix} 7 & 15 \\ -5 & 39 \end{vmatrix} = 273 + 75 = 348\)

The single chain gives two equations.

From \(\dfrac{x + y - 8}{2} = \dfrac{x + 2y - 14}{3}\): \(3(x + y - 8) = 2(x + 2y - 14)\)

\(\therefore 3x + 3y - 24 = 2x + 4y - 28\) \(\therefore x - y = -4\) . . . (I)

From \(\dfrac{x + 2y - 14}{3} = \dfrac{3x - y}{4}\): \(4(x + 2y - 14) = 3(3x - y)\)

\(\therefore 4x + 8y - 56 = 9x - 3y\) \(\therefore -5x + 11y = 56\) . . . (II)

\(\mathrm{D} = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ -5 & 11 \end{vmatrix} = 11 - 5 = 6\)

\(\mathrm{D}_x = \begin{vmatrix} -4 & -1 \\ 56 & 11 \end{vmatrix} = -44 + 56 = 12\)

\(\mathrm{D}_y = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -4 \\ -5 & 56 \end{vmatrix} = 56 - 20 = 36\)

\(x = \dfrac{12}{6} = 2\), \(y = \dfrac{36}{6} = 6\)

Let the digit in unit's place be \(x\) and the digit in the ten's place be \(y\).

\(\therefore\) the number is \(10y + x\), and the number with digits interchanged is \(10x + y\).

\(\therefore 11x + 11y = 143\) \(\therefore x + y = 13\) . . . (I)

From the second condition: \(x = y + 3\) \(\therefore x - y = 3\) . . . (II)

Let the rate of tea be ₹ \(x\) per kg and the rate of sugar be ₹ \(y\) per kg.

In the shop Kantabai spent ₹ 700 in all, of which ₹ 50 was the rickshaw fare, so the goods cost \(700 - 50 = 650\) rupees.

\(\dfrac{3}{2}x + 5y = 650\), i.e. \(3x + 10y = 1300\) . . . (I)

Online there is no fare, so \(2x + 7y = 880\) . . . (II)

Multiplying equation (I) by 2 and equation (II) by 3:

\(6x + 20y = 2600\) . . . (III)

\(6x + 21y = 2640\) . . . (IV)

Subtracting equation (III) from equation (IV): \(y = 40\)

From equation (II): \(2x = 880 - 280 = 600\) \(\therefore x = 300\)

\(\therefore\) tea costs ₹ 300 per kg and sugar costs ₹ 40 per kg.

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

Suppose Anushka had \(x\) notes of ₹ 100 and \(y\) notes of ₹ 50.

Equation II (the amount with the number of notes interchanged, which is ₹ 500 less): \(100y + 50x = 2000\), i.e. \(x + 2y = 40\) . . . (II)

Multiplying equation (I) by 2: \(4x + 2y = 100\) . . . (III)

Subtracting equation (II) from equation (III): \(3x = 60\) \(\therefore x = 20\)

From equation (I): \(y = 50 - 40 = 10\)

\(\therefore\) Anushka had 20 notes of ₹ 100 and 10 notes of ₹ 50.

This agrees with the answer printed in the book's ANSWERS section.

Let Hamid's speed be \(x\) km/hr and Joseph's speed be \(y\) km/hr.

Moving towards each other they close the 30 km gap at \((x + y)\) km/hr and meet after 20 minutes \(= \dfrac{1}{3}\) hour.

\((x + y) \times \dfrac{1}{3} = 30\) \(\therefore x + y = 90\) . . . (I)

Moving in the same direction Hamid closes the 30 km gap at \((x - y)\) km/hr and catches Joseph after 3 hours.

\((x - y) \times 3 = 30\) \(\therefore x - y = 10\) . . . (II)

Adding: \(2x = 100\) \(\therefore x = 50\); then \(y = 40\)

\(\therefore\) Hamid's speed is 50 km/hr and Joseph's speed is 40 km/hr.
